plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Focus on capital preservation and broad market exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month, but actual returns are not guaranteed. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Reduce exposure to all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to small positions.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure to growth.
Buy XLV at 4% to diversify into a high-scoring, non-tech sector.
This plan balances risk and growth, aiming for a more stable portfolio.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by blending broad index, quality tech, and reduced leverage. It aims for risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer. Expect controlled drawdowns and a more diversified risk profile compared to the current book.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to 6% each.
This strategy leans into high-beta, high-growth sectors.
Buy XLV at 6% as a top-scoring scanner setup.
This plan aims to stretch growth by using leverage and concentration.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by leveraging high-growth sectors and top scanner setups. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if not managed with strict stop discipline.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
This shifts the portfolio focus heavily towards income generation.
Prioritize low drawdown and reliable monthly distributions.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index funds. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions over growth. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
